source_text: Τοὺς δὲ τὴν ἐντολὴν πληροῦντας, ἐκτὸς πάσης αἰσχροκερδείας πληροῦν δεῖ, μήτε μήνυτρα ἢ σῶστρα ἢ εὕρετρα ἢ ᾧ ὀνόματι ταῦτα καλοῦσιν ἀπαιτοῦντας.
thought_title: Instruction for those fulfilling the commandment without greed
orientation: Gregory instructs the bishop that those who fulfill the commandment must do so without any form of shameful gain, forbidding demands for informer fees, rewards for seizure, or finder's fees under any name.
pass_a_gloss: But those fulfilling the commandment, it is necessary [for them] to fulfill [it] outside of all shameful gain, not demanding informer fees or rewards for seizure or finder's fees or by whatever name these things are called.

lemmas.gloss: fulfilling, carrying out (present active participle accusative plural masculine)
shameful gain, greed for base profit (genitive singular feminine)
to fulfill, carry out (present active infinitive)
it is necessary, one must (impersonal verb)
informer's fee, reward for informing (accusative singular neuter)
reward for saving/seizing, salvage fee (accusative singular neuter)
finder's fee, reward for finding (accusative singular neuter)
by which, with which (dative singular neuter)
they call, are called (present active indicative 3rd plural)
demanding, exacting (present active participle accusative plural masculine)

choices.english: it is necessary [for them] to fulfill
choices.why: The construction δεῖ + infinitive expresses necessity; the subject of the infinitive is the same as the participle 'those fulfilling' carried over from the main clause.
ἐκτὸς + genitive means 'outside of' or 'apart from'; αἰσχροκέρδεια is a specific term for shameful or base profit, not general greed.

choices.english: informer fees or rewards for seizure or finder's fees
choices.why: These are three distinct technical terms for types of rewards: μήνυτρον for informing, σῶστρον for saving/seizing, εὕρετρον for finding. Each must be distinguished.
rejected: informant fees or salvage or finder's fees

choices.english: by whatever name these things are called
choices.why: Dative of reference ᾧ ὀνόματι 'by what name'; the relative clause covers any other designation for such payments.
rejected: under whatever name they go by

choices.why: Present active participle agreeing with the implied subject of πληροῦν; indicates the active stance of requiring payment as a condition.

pass_b_english: Those who carry out the command must fulfill it without any shameful gain, refusing to demand informer fees, seizure rewards, finder's fees, or payments by whatever name these things are called.
